_meta.decisionRule: Trust neither side; live-probe truth; cross-check against runtime code

expectedProductCount.evidence: Live: GET /wp-json/wp/v2/product?per_page=1 -> x-wp-total: 2808 (2026-05-13 08:44Z). DB stored 2756 (stale snapshot from 2026-04-11). R1 chose 1586 (Store API customer-visible). Both stale or wrong-source; live truth is 2808. Choosing WP REST (broader, all-published) per DB design intent for back-in-stock alerting.

productCountMethod.evidence: Two reasons to choose WP REST over Store API: (1) WC Store API hides OOS (1586 vs 2808 = 1222 hidden), and back-in-stock alerting requires the broader population. (2) Runtime woocommerce.ts:340 calls /wp-json/wp/v2/product for both discovery and watermark, so count source matches crawl source. R1's choice followed SKILL.md priority naively. DB choice correct.

value.evidence: Live 2026-05-13: ?after=2099 -> 0; ?after=1999 -> 2808; ?modified_after=2099 -> 0; ?modified_after=1999 -> 2808. KEY: ?after=last-7d -> 7 NEW products; ?modified_after=last-7d -> 311 products. modified_after catches 304 stock/price updates the after filter misses.

apiDateFilter.evidence: Runtime woocommerce.ts:337 hardcodes params.modified_after = options.dateAfter (not after). Empirical 44x difference at 7d window proves modified_after is the right field for restock-detection. R1's ?after= mention in `reason` string is misleading because runtime never sends that param.

catalogUrls.evidence: BOTH WRONG, R1 closer. DB's [/products/] yields 0 products via woocommerce.extractCatalogProducts at runtime (live verified - /products/ is Woodmart AJAX, only sidebar widget refs in static HTML). DB's htmlCrawlViable=false flag NOT consumed by runtime (grep confirmed zero refs in src/services). R1's 22 URLs work: 17 leaf categories extract 12 products per page from p1. The 5 parent-tile categories yield 0 on p1 (wd-with-subcat) but products appear from p2 (verified: ammunition p2 = 12 via adapter; pal-ups walked 18 pages = ~225 products vs Store API 213). Playwright fallback at catalog-crawler.ts:435 handles 5 parent-tile p1 cases.

htmlCrawlViable.evidence: DB declared false; R1 implicitly true. Live: woocommerce adapter extracts 12 products per leaf-category page (pal-ups p1-p18 walked cleanly). DB note 'Woodmart AJAX shop, only 5 sidebar widgets' is correct ONLY for /products/, not for /product-category/<slug>/page/N/. R1 correct; DB applied a /products/-specific observation to the wrong scope.

paginationPattern.evidence: DB's type=api-page + template=page={N} falls through to default query in buildPaginatedUrl (catalog-crawler.ts:118-165 has no api-page branch), producing /products/?page=2 (wrong: WC uses /page/N/ path). R1's type=path + template=/page/{N}/ matches catalog-crawler path-type handler and live HTML pagination. Live: ?per_page=100 honored at /product-category/pal-ups/page/2/?per_page=100 (100 products extracted).

crawlersBootstrap.evidence: Documentation-only field; runtime grep confirms 0 references to crawlers.bootstrap.method, apiEndpoints, htmlFallback in backend/src/services. R1 used keys wpRestProduct/wcStoreProducts; DB keys productDiscovery/priceEnrichment are more descriptive. Keep DB shape.

sortVerifiedMethod.evidence: Live 2026-05-13: page1 first id=97796 last id=95713; page2 first id=95706. Monotonically descending across page boundary. DB choice canonical for WC sites (actual API data > HTML counter-control). R1's HTML 3-outcome would also pass but API-level proof is stronger.

htmlCrawlNote.value: Woodmart theme: /products/ shop page is AJAX-loaded (woodmart-ajax-shop-on), only 5 sidebar widget refs in static HTML. BUT /product-category/<slug>/page/N/ DOES render static product grids (12 per page via .wd-product). 5 of 22 categories have parent-tile mode on page 1 (wd-with-subcat) - those pages yield 0 products but real products appear from page 2 onward. Catalog-crawler Playwright fallback at line 435 handles those 5 page-1 cases.
htmlCrawlNote.evidence: Refined DB note (correct for /products/ but mis-applied as universal). R1 omitted any note.

perPage.evidence: Live: ?per_page=100 honored on /product-category/pal-ups/page/2/ - returned 100 unique product links. Both DB and R1 agree. Confirmed.

_categoryRecursionFinding.evidence: Live 2026-05-13: GET /wp-json/wp/v2/product?per_page=1&product_cat=162 -> x-wp-total: 5 (direct-assigned only). GET /wp-json/wc/store/v1/products?per_page=1&category=162 -> x-wp-total: 98 (recurses into 12 children). 19.6x difference. Validates DB catalogUrlsNote.
_categoryRecursionFinding.implication: If operator switches catalog crawl to per-category WP REST product_cat=N filter, coverage collapses 95% silently. DB chose global /wp/v2/product crawl with no category filter. R1's HTML walk approach sidesteps the issue because HTML category pages render full descendant product set.

_filterParamFinding.evidence: ?after=last-7d -> 7 products; ?modified_after=last-7d -> 311 products. At 30d: ?after=42 vs ?modified_after=821. modified_after captures NEW + UPDATED (stock/price/restock); after captures NEW only.
_filterParamFinding.runtimeBinding: woocommerce.ts:337 hardcodes params.modified_after = options.dateAfter. The site profile apiDateFilter.param value is descriptive metadata; actual runtime always uses modified_after.
_filterParamFinding.skillMdGap: SKILL.md Stage 7 ONLY mentions ?after= probe. For WooCommerce, modified_after is the canonical watermark filter.
